scenario.prompt_to_agent:
All Campus 2 PCs (PC1-4, dc_pc5) report they cannot reach
Campus 1 or the WAN. They CAN still ping their own gateways
(10.5.0.254, 10.6.0.254) on sshswitch. Find what cut Campus 2's
uplink.

injection.action: bring down the bond toward router17 (eth6+eth7)

post_inject_check.command: ip link show bond0 | grep -c "state DOWN"

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch bond0 (LACP to router17)
Mechanism: bond0 is sshswitch's only L3 uplink toward router17,
  carrying tagged VLAN 100 (servers — excluded from hosts),
  VLAN 200, and untagged VLAN 1 traffic toward the OSPF
  backbone. With bond0 down, sshswitch loses OSPF adjacency
  with router17 and Campus 2 becomes an island. Local gateways
  still respond because they're SVIs on sshswitch itself.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: bond0 (port-channel toward router17) is down on sshswitch
Fix: `ip link set bond0 up` on sshswitch
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set bond0 up` on sshswitch

line.command: ip link show bond0 | grep -c "state DOWN"

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault lies in the EtherChannel (bonded) uplink interface `bond0` on sshswitch,
which connects the Campus 2 multilayer switch to router17 via the `r17_ms1` /
`r17_ms1_2` links (sshswitch eth6 + eth7).

Bond0 is in an administratively DOWN state (Linux flags show no UP/LOWER_UP on the
bond interface itself, only on its slave members). Both physical slaves (eth6 and
eth7) report MII Status: up in /proc/net/bonding/bond0 and show LOWER_UP in ip
link — confirming the physical wiring is intact. The startup.sh explicitly issues
`ip link set bond0 up`, so the bond was brought up at boot and was later shut down
by the injected fault (`ip link set bond0 down`).

As a result:
• All bond0.X VLAN subinterfaces (bond0.5, bond0.6, bond0.100, bond0.200) are
  M-DOWN, disabling the 802.1Q trunk path to router17.
• Sshswitch cannot reach router17's bond0 IP (55.5.1.1): 100% packet loss
  confirmed by direct ping.
• OSPF running on sshswitch has zero neighbors on every interface — it is sending
  hellos only into the Campus 2 side via eth0 (the switch4 downlink sharing br_v1),
  never reaching router17. Router17 correspondingly has no OSPF adjacency on bond0
  and no routes for any Campus 2 subnet (10.5.0.0/24, 10.6.0.0/24, etc.).
• Sshswitch itself holds only directly connected routes (its local VLANs) and no
  default or inter-campus routes, so any packet from a Campus 2 PC whose
  destination is outside those local subnets is silently dropped at sshswitch.
• The gateways (10.5.0.254, 10.6.0.254) remain pingable because br_v5 and br_v6
  are still UP via the eth0.5/eth0.6 access paths through switch4.

Root cause: bond0 on sshswitch was administratively shut down, severing the
sole uplink to router17 and collapsing all OSPF routing for Campus 2.

Corrective fix: On sshswitch, run `ip link set bond0 up`. This restores the trunk
to router17, re-establishes the OSPF adjacency on the 55.5.1.0/24 link, and within
one OSPF dead-interval the full inter-campus and WAN routing table will repopulate
on sshswitch and router17 will learn the Campus 2 prefixes.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names sshswitch as the affected device and describes its bond0 interface and behavior.
Agent explicitly identifies bond0—the bonded/port-channel uplink on sshswitch to router17—as the failed component.
The report explicitly states that the local SVIs/gateways remain pingable (br_v5/br_v6 UP via eth0.5/eth0.6), distinguishing local connectivity from the broken uplink.
Recommends running `ip link set bond0 up` on sshswitch, which exactly matches the expected corrective action.

The log shows bond0 on sshswitch is down while its slaves are up, OSPF neighbors are absent on sshswitch, the router-side adjacency is missing, and ping to the router IP fails — supporting the agent's conclusion that an administratively-down bond0 severed the uplink and OSPF. Some peripheral claims (e.g. explicit absence of Campus-2 routes on router17) are implied but not fully shown in the snippets.
